I added `DELETE /api/v1/items/{id}/description`. It clears the item's description and returns the updated item. I did not run the tests or the app, as you asked.

Changes:

- **`backend/app/crud.py`**: added `get_item` and `clear_item_description`. The second sets `description` to `None`, commits, refreshes, and returns the item.
- **`backend/app/api/routes/items.py`**: added the route after `delete_item`. It returns 404 `"Item not found"` when the item is missing and 403 `"Not enough permissions"` when the caller is neither the owner nor a superuser. The same checks as the other item routes apply.

The route returns `ItemPublic`, so the response matches `GET /items/{id}`. Following the project's lint rules, the route reaches the database only through `crud.py`, and it uses `status` constants for the error codes.

Things to know:

- The project's API doc says `DELETE` returns a `Message`. I followed your request to return the updated item instead, so this endpoint deviates from that convention.
- The frontend client is generated from the OpenAPI schema. Run `bash scripts/generate-client.sh` to pick up the new operation. I did not run it, since it starts the app's schema generation.
- Nothing is committed.
